village.title: Village Kinship Web (1747–1973)
village.subtitle: Ten interlocking parish families reconstructed from St Peter’s registers, 1841–1921 censuses, wills, and churchyard memorials.

nodes.name: Mary Allen
nodes.notes: Born High Wycombe c. 1771. Listed in Lockington censuses 1841–1861 (erroneously recorded aged 99 in 1861; actually 90). Lived with granddaughter Emma Burnham in 1851 and in Joseph & Lydia Burnham’s house in 1861.

nodes.name: Joseph Burnham
nodes.notes: Born Ilmer/Kingsey c. 1813; married Lydia Allen at St Peter’s on 17 Oct 1838. Lived at Lockington (1841–1861) and Ilmer (1871–1881). Buried 13 Jan 1890 aged 77.

nodes.name: Lydia Allen
nodes.notes: Married Joseph Burnham in 1838. Confirmed as daughter of Mary Allen via the 1851 Lockington census (Emma Burnham listed as Mary Allen’s granddaughter) and 1861 co-residence.

nodes.name: James Burnham
nodes.notes: Baptized 3 Aug 1845 (son of Joseph & Lydia Burnham; brother of Emma, Charlotte, William, Matilda & Frederick). Married Kate (d. 1891 age 32). Lived with widowed father Joseph in 1881.

nodes.name: William, Robert & Joseph Burnham
nodes.notes: Sons of James & Kate Burnham. William James (age 3mo) is explicitly listed as "Grandson" in Joseph Burnham’s 1881 household.

members.name: William James Burnham
members.notes: Aged 3 months in 1881 census as grandson in Joseph Burnham’s household.

members.name: Robert G Burnham
members.notes: Aged 9 in 1891 census and 19 in 1901 census.

members.name: Joseph E Burnham
members.notes: Aged 5 in 1891 census and 15 in 1901 census.

nodes.name: Thomas Horton
nodes.notes: Married Sarah Southall at St Peter’s on 2 Dec 1770 (witnessed by Thomas Kingham).

nodes.name: Sarah Southall
nodes.notes: Married Thomas Horton in 1770; buried at Ilmer 10 Jan 1823 aged 69.

nodes.name: William Horton
nodes.notes: Baptized 11 May 1777; buried 29 Jul 1831 aged 54 (exact age match). With wife Elizabeth (b. c. 1786) had at least 10 children baptized 1804–1829.

nodes.name: Elizabeth Horton
nodes.notes: Baptized 3 Apr 1807 (daughter of William & Elizabeth Horton). Married John Allen of Ilmer on 15 Oct 1832 (witnessed by sister Frances Horton).

nodes.name: Susanna Horton
nodes.notes: Baptized 31 May 1818. Living with widowed mother Elizabeth Horton and 2-year-old son John in the 1841 census; also had daughter Emma (bap. 1844).

nodes.name: John Horton
nodes.notes: Baptized 24 Mar 1839 (son of Susanna Horton); age 2 in 1841, age 32 in 1871 census (born Ilmer) with wife Emma (b. Princes Risborough c. 1840).

nodes.name: 8 Horton Children (Gen 5)
nodes.notes: Children of John & Emma Horton: Thomas (c. 1861), Frederick (1865), Louisa (c. 1867), Isabella August (1870), Owen (1872–1872), John James (1873), Arthur Edward (1876), Elizabeth Jane (1879).

members.name: Owen Horton
members.notes: Buried aged 5 weeks.

nodes.name: Richard Stratford
nodes.notes: With wife Sarah had 8+ children baptized at St Peter’s between 1792 and 1825 (several baptized as adults in May 1820). Buried 3 Oct 1837 aged 77, widower.

nodes.name: Theodosia Kingham
nodes.notes: Born Towersey c. 1787. Living in Ilmer in 1871 aged 84 as "Mother" in the household of widowed daughter Hannah Stratford. Buried 31 May 1871 aged 83.

nodes.name: William Stratford
nodes.notes: Baptized as an adult on 21 May 1820 (son of Richard & Sarah Stratford). Married Anna/Hannah Kingham on 13 Oct 1833. Buried 16 Aug 1868.

nodes.name: Hannah (Anna) Kingham
nodes.notes: Daughter of Theodosia Kingham (co-resident in 1871). Married William Stratford 13 Oct 1833; had 9 children. Buried 8 May 1886 aged 72.

nodes.name: Sophia Stratford (Matthews)
nodes.notes: Daughter of William & Hannah Stratford (sibling of Benjamin, Sarah, Elizabeth, Fanny, John d. 1918, Eliza, Emma, Thomas). Widowed by 1911, living at Lower Farm Cottage with brother John Stratford and daughter Emma Matthews.

nodes.name: Emma Matthews
nodes.notes: Recorded as "Niece" (age 14) of John Stratford and daughter of widowed Sophia Matthews (née Stratford) in the 1911 census.

nodes.name: George Stratford
nodes.notes: Explicitly recorded as "Grandson" (age 1 in 1861, age 10 in 1871) in William & Hannah Stratford’s household in Ilmer.

nodes.name: Richard Clare
nodes.notes: Born Thame; married Elizabeth (b. Oakley, Oxon c. 1794). Had 7+ children baptized at Ilmer (1819–1835). Buried 19 Mar 1857 aged 69.

nodes.name: James Clare
nodes.notes: Baptized 23 Nov 1834 (son of Richard & Elizabeth Clare). Married Eliza Pitchford on 31 Jul 1862; had 9 children baptized/recorded 1862–1881.

nodes.name: 9 Clare Children
nodes.notes: Children of James & Eliza Clare: Ann, James, Emily, Richard (all bap. 6 Jun 1869), Elizabeth (1871), Mary & Elizabeth (1874), Arthur (1876), Ada (1879), and an infant son (1881).

members.name: Infant Clare
members.notes: Recorded as 1-month-old infant son in the 1881 census.

nodes.name: Ann Clare
nodes.notes: Baptized 13 Dec 1835 (daughter of Richard & Elizabeth Clare). Married James Kingham on 23 Nov 1856 aged 21. Died 3 Mar 1900 aged 62 (headstone B2).

nodes.name: Joshua Kingham (the elder)
nodes.notes: Left a detailed transcribed will dated 22 Feb 1779 (proved 6 Jul 1779) naming son John (sole executor) and daughters Mary, Sarah, Elizabeth, Hannah, Ann West, and Jane.

nodes.name: Sarah Kingham
nodes.notes: Wife of Joshua Kingham the elder; mother of seven children baptized at St Peter’s between 1751 and 1764.

nodes.name: John Kingham
nodes.notes: Married Hannah Kingham at Ilmer on 9 Jun 1777 ("both otp"). Buried 22 Aug 1810 ("farmer"); yeoman will proved 1811. Multiple contemporary John Kinghams (bap. 1744, 1752, 1755) exist in Ilmer registers.

nodes.name: Hannah Kingham
nodes.notes: Married John Kingham 9 Jun 1777; buried 12 Jun 1803 ("wife of John"). Very likely the daughter Hannah baptized 14 Apr 1757 to Joshua Kingham the elder (who left £40 to "daughter Hannah Kingham" in 1779).

nodes.name: Joshua Kingham
nodes.notes: Baptized 10 Jan 1798 (son of John & Hannah Kingham). With wife Hannah/Anna (b. c. 1803 Great Kimble, d. 1876 age 73) had twins John & James (1828), William (1830), Charles (1834), George (1839), and Eliza (1841).

nodes.name: James Kingham
nodes.notes: Baptized 12 Oct 1828 (twin of John; son of Joshua & Hannah Kingham). Married Ann Clare in 1856; died 10 Nov 1907 aged 79 (headstone B2).

nodes.name: William Kingham
nodes.notes: Son of James Kingham & Ann Clare (age 2 in 1861, 12 servant in 1871, 22 in 1881, then head at Close End 1891–1921). Married Elizabeth Claydon (c. 1863–1939, featured in the 1935 Daily Sketch). Buried 25 Apr 1929 aged 70.

nodes.name: Albert Andrew Kingham
nodes.notes: Baptized 7 Aug 1887 (son of William Kingham & Elizabeth Claydon; brother of Ernest George bap. 1890). Married Florence Allen (1887–1980) on 11 Nov 1911. Died 29 Jan 1969 aged 81 (headstone B3).

nodes.name: Doris Mary Kingham (Rixon)
nodes.notes: Born Sep 1919, baptized 12 Oct 1919 (twin of Elsie Margaret; daughter of Albert Andrew Kingham & Florence Allen). Married lorry driver Reginald John Rixon at St Peter’s on 6 Jan 1940 aged 20.

nodes.name: Robin John (1941) & Judy Ann Rixon (1943)
nodes.notes: Children of Reginald John Rixon & Doris Mary (née Kingham), baptized at St Peter’s on 22 Jun 1941 and 10 Oct 1943 — the 7th unbroken generation from John & Hannah Kingham (m. 1777) and 6th from Richard Clare.

nodes.name: James & Sarah Wooster
nodes.notes: James (b. c. 1810 Missenden) & Sarah (b. c. 1813 Monks Risborough) farmed 137 acres in Ilmer and raised 12 children, linking by marriage to Kingham (1854), Goodchild (1865), and Goff.

members.name: Sarah Wooster
members.notes: Widowed by 1871, farming in Ilmer with five children and granddaughter Mary Kingham.

nodes.name: Anna (Anne) Wooster
nodes.notes: Daughter of James & Sarah Wooster (bap. 18 Aug 1839). Married James Kingham on 17 Dec 1854; their daughter Mary Kingham (age 16) lived with grandmother Sarah Wooster in 1871.

nodes.name: Mary Kingham
nodes.notes: Explicitly listed as "Granddaughter" (age 16) in widow Sarah Wooster’s 1871 household following Anna Wooster’s 1854 marriage to James Kingham.

nodes.name: Joseph Wooster
nodes.notes: Son of James & Sarah Wooster (born Ilmer c. 1847). Married Hannah North on 14 Apr 1873; six children baptized 1887–1888.

nodes.name: Edith Wooster (Goff)
nodes.notes: Baptized 27 Nov 1887 with four siblings (daughter of Joseph & Hannah Wooster). Married William Goff (Soldier, 1st Life Guards); staying at Joseph Wooster’s Ilmer home in 1901 with two children.

nodes.name: William George Goff
nodes.notes: Baptized at St Peter’s 24 Mar 1901 ("Windsor Lifeguards"); enumerated aged 2 months at grandfather Joseph Wooster’s house in Ilmer in 1901. Later lived at 55 Coronation Buildings, Vauxhall.

nodes.name: Alan George (1927) & Ruth Mary Goff (1928)
nodes.notes: Brought back from Vauxhall, London to be baptized at St Peter’s, Ilmer on 17 Apr 1927 and 15 Jul 1928 — completing 5 verified generations from James & Sarah Wooster.

nodes.name: Fanny Wooster
nodes.notes: Daughter of James & Sarah Wooster. Married Thomas Goodchild of Longwick (aged 21, an earlier Thomas Goodchild distinct from David’s son) on 14 Mar 1865.

nodes.name: Jane Kingham
nodes.notes: Youngest daughter of Joshua Kingham the elder (under 21 in his 1779 will, granted board and lodging with her brother John). Married James Goodchild at Ilmer on 4 Jul 1790.

nodes.name: James Goodchild
nodes.notes: Married Jane Kingham on 4 Jul 1790; their daughter Sarah Goodchild was baptized 11 Aug 1790 and buried 6 Sep 1790.

nodes.name: David & Elizabeth Goodchild
nodes.notes: Moved from Longwick to the Old Vicarage, Ilmer by 1873; raised 9 children. Tragedy struck in Dec 1885 (Elizabeth died age 53) and Dec 1886 (David died of a heart attack age 55), leaving eldest sons Thomas & John to raise the younger boys.

members.name: David Goodchild
members.notes: Died of a heart attack in Dec 1886 aged 55.

members.name: Elizabeth Goodchild
members.notes: Died in Dec 1885 aged 53.

nodes.name: John Goodchild
nodes.notes: Co-executor of father David Goodchild’s will. Married Lucy Kingham (age 21) at St Peter’s on 15 Sep 1877; four children baptized 1879–1889.

nodes.name: Thomas Goodchild
nodes.notes: Executor of father David’s will aged 22; moved to the Old Vicarage with wife Mary (1861–1933) to raise orphaned younger brothers Albert, Owen & Ernest. Died 3 Oct 1930 aged 67 (headstone C19).

nodes.name: Albert Goodchild
nodes.notes: Orphaned at 13; married Elizabeth Mason (1894), built a thriving Covent Garden flower business, bought Upper Farm in 1909 to build Ilmer House, and bought the Old Vicarage in 1927. Died 15 Jul 1931 aged 57 (Celtic cross C11).

nodes.name: Owen (1876–1932) & Ernest (1878)
nodes.notes: Owen (bap. 1876, d. 1932, headstone C18 with wife Kate Louisa; dau Dorothy Isabel bap. 1904) and Ernest William (bap. 1878, departed Liverpool aged 13 in 1892 as a British Home Child to Winnipeg, Canada).

members.name: Owen Goodchild
members.notes: Married Kate Louisa (d. 1935); daughter Dorothy Isabel baptized 28 Feb 1904. Headstone C18.

members.name: Ernest William Goodchild
members.notes: Departed Liverpool aged 13 in 1892 as a British Home Child bound for Quebec and Winnipeg.

nodes.name: Harry Goodchild
nodes.notes: Baptized 24 Mar 1889 (son of Thomas & Mary Goodchild; brother of Louise, Frank, Ethel, Doris & Ada). Married Annie Smith (1890–1964, pictured in the 1935 Daily Sketch) on 27 Apr 1918. Died 26 Apr 1973 aged 84 (headstone C20).

nodes.name: (Robert) Douglas Goodchild
nodes.notes: Youngest child of Albert & Elizabeth Goodchild. Lived at the Old Vicarage and built the glasshouse nursery in central Ilmer (now Ilmer Meadows) before its 1946 closure.

nodes.name: Winifred, Elsie, Florence & Ernest John
nodes.notes: Children of Harry & Annie Goodchild: Winifred May (1919, m. Matthews 1942), Elsie Dorothy (1921, pictured in the 1935 Daily Sketch, m. Gerald Knight), Florence Mary (1925, m. Miller 1948), and Ernest John (1929–1968, headstone C17).

members.name: Winifred May Goodchild
members.notes: Married Vincent Charles Matthews at St Peter’s on 21 Oct 1942.

members.name: Elsie Dorothy Goodchild
members.notes: Pictured in the 1935 Daily Sketch feature on Ilmer; married Gerald Knight.

members.name: Florence Mary Goodchild
members.notes: Married Leslie Joseph Miller at St Peter’s on 23 Oct 1948.

members.name: Ernest John Goodchild
members.notes: Died aged 39; headstone C17.

nodes.name: John Gomme
nodes.notes: Grazier of Cold Harbour, Ilmer. Buried 17 Apr 1771; will proved 1771. With wife Mary had five children baptized 1747–1759.

nodes.name: John Gomme
nodes.notes: Baptized 27 Oct 1750, buried 2 Jan 1825 aged 75 (exact match). Had 3 children by 1st wife Elizabeth (d. 1788) and 10 children (1793–1815) by 2nd wife Hannah (b. c. 1771 Towersey).

nodes.name: Hannah Gomme
nodes.notes: Born Towersey c. 1771; 2nd wife of John Gomme. Head of Cold Harbour dairy farm as widow in 1841 (age 70) and 1851 (age 80), hosting daughter Hannah and nephews Alfred & Eli.

nodes.name: Edwin Gomme
nodes.notes: Youngest child of John & Hannah Gomme (bap. 30 Jul 1815). Married Eliza Goodchild at St Peter’s on 19 Dec 1839; five children baptized 1840–1849.

nodes.name: Anne Gomm
nodes.notes: Eldest child of John & Hannah Gomme (bap. 24 Feb 1793). Married Thomas Kingham of Ilmer on 28 Feb 1811 (witnessed by Hannah Gomm).

nodes.name: Jesse Gomme
nodes.notes: Baptized 29 Nov 1798; buried 18 Dec 1867 aged 68. Tenant of the Old Vicarage in the 1839 tithe map and 1841–1861 censuses with wife Charlotte (b. Bledlow c. 1808).

nodes.name: Esther Gomme
nodes.notes: Baptized 16 Jul 1809. Mother of Anne Gome (bap. 24 Jun 1832); married William Bowden of Towersey on 2 May 1833.

nodes.name: Henry & Hannah Gomme
nodes.notes: Siblings Henry (bap. 1801, d. 1879 age 78, m. Sarah Jane Curryer 1835) and unmarried sister Hannah (bap. 1794, d. 1884 age 90) farmed Cold Harbour together. Commemorated together on headstone C14.

members.name: Henry Gomme
members.notes: Married Sarah Jane Curryer (1835). Commemorated on headstone C14.

members.name: Hannah Gomme
members.notes: Unmarried sister of Henry; farmed Cold Harbour and died aged 90. Headstone C14.

nodes.name: Eli Gomme
nodes.notes: Son of Jesse & Charlotte Gomme. Married his first cousin Anne Gomme on 14 Sep 1850; lived at Cold Harbour with grandmother Hannah in 1851.

nodes.name: Anne Gomme
nodes.notes: Baptized 24 Jun 1832 (daughter of Esther Gomme); raised with grandmother Hannah Gomme in 1841. Married cousin Eli Gomme in 1850.

nodes.name: William Henry Gomme
nodes.notes: Baptized 26 Jan 1851 (son of cousins Eli & Anne Gomme; brother of Mary Anne 1852 & Hannah 1859). Age 3mo in 1851, age 21 "Nephew" at Cold Harbour in 1871. Married Anne Wagerfield on 29 May 1873.

nodes.name: George & Hannah Julia Gomme
nodes.notes: Born Bledlow c. 1865; listed as "Grandson" of Henry Gomme (1871) and "Nephew" of Hannah Gomme (1881), succeeding them as Cold Harbour farmer. Had 10 children with Hannah Julia (headstone C8).

members.name: George Gomme
members.notes: Listed as Henry Gomme’s grandson (1871) and Hannah Gomme’s nephew (1881). Died aged 80; headstone C8.

members.name: Hannah Julia Gomme
members.notes: Wife of George Gomme; died aged 68. Headstone C8.

nodes.name: Aubrey Sidney Gomme
nodes.notes: Born at Coldharbour Farm 20 Aug 1892; emigrated to Canada in 1911 and served with the 21st Canadian Battalion. Killed in action at Vimy Ridge on 9 Apr 1917 aged 24; commemorated on Ilmer’s War Memorial.

nodes.name: Philip, Ettie & 7 Siblings
nodes.notes: Siblings of Aubrey: Harry Herbert (1890–1970), Elsie Beatrice (1892–1968), Philip William (b. 1895), Winifred (1898), Dorothy (1900), Ettie Nellie (1902–1907, fatally shot by accident in the granary), Lena (1905), Arthur (1908–09), Lilian (1910).

members.name: Ettie Nellie Gomme
members.notes: Died aged 5 in the accidental granary shooting at Cold Harbour Farm.

members.name: Arthur Frederick Gomme
members.notes: Buried aged 1 year.

nodes.name: Richard & Martha Belgrove
nodes.notes: Richard (b. Stewkley c. 1830) & Martha Rudd (b. Weedon c. 1840) farmed Upper Farm (now Ilmer House) for decades (1871–1901 censuses) and raised 9+ children including church organist Martha and "Ilmer Hermit" Charles.

nodes.name: Charlotte Belgrove (Claydon)
nodes.notes: Baptized 30 Dec 1866 (daughter of Richard & Martha Belgrove). Married grocer John Thomas Claydon (1865–1936) on 29 Dec 1888. Died 14 Nov 1943 aged 77 (headstone C21).

nodes.name: Charles & Martha Belgrove
nodes.notes: Charles ("The Ilmer Hermit", b. 1885, d. Nov 1968/bur. Feb 1969) lived alone at Lockington for 66 years after falling out with his father. Sister Martha (d. 1909 age 44) was St Peter’s organist for 25 years (window A2, headstone C22).

members.name: Charles Belgrove
members.notes: Lived alone at Lockington for 66 years after falling out with his father; died aged 84.

members.name: Martha Belgrove
members.notes: Organist at St Peter’s for 25 years; commemorated by stained-glass window A2 and headstone C22.

nodes.name: David & Mark Claydon
nodes.notes: Sons of John Thomas Claydon & Charlotte Belgrove (brothers of Esther 1890, Ruth 1894–1937 [C21], Mary 1896). David (m. Constance Mary, headstone B4) and Mark (m. Freda, headstone B5) are both buried at St Peter’s.

members.name: David Claydon
members.notes: Married Constance Mary (d. 1977); headstone B4.

members.name: Mark Claydon
members.notes: Married Freda (1915–1981); headstone B5.

nodes.name: Mary Ann Claydon (Warren)
nodes.notes: Born 4 Nov 1931, baptized 3 Apr 1932 (daughter of David & Constance Mary Claydon). Married Norman Leonard Warren at St Peter’s on 2 Apr 1960.

manor.title: Manorial & Landowning Dynasties (1338–1912)
manor.subtitle: Three successive noble and gentry lineages holding the Manor of Ilmer across six centuries.

nodes.name: Sir John & Lady Egidia de Moleyns
nodes.notes: Held the Manor of Ilmer in serjeanty (1338) as Marshal and Keeper of the King’s Hawks; granted licence to enclose Ilmer woods as a park in 1336.

members.name: Lady Egidia de Moleyns
members.notes: Widow of Sir John de Moleyns; held Ilmer until her death in Jan 1366/67.

nodes.name: Sir William de Moleyns
nodes.notes: Surviving son of Sir John & Lady Egidia; inherited Ilmer on his mother’s death in Jan 1366/67.

nodes.name: Sir Richard de Moleyns
nodes.notes: Died 14 Dec 1384 leaving his heir William de Moleyns aged 7.

nodes.name: Sir William de Moleyns
nodes.notes: Died 8 Jun 1425; his Oct 1425 Inquisition post mortem surveyed 160 arable acres, 21 acres meadow, and pasture "le Grove" in Ilmer.

nodes.name: Sir William de Moleyns
nodes.notes: Killed 8 May 1429 at the Siege of Orléans during the Hundred Years’ War; succeeded by his 3-year-old only daughter Eleanor.

nodes.name: Eleanor (Alianor) de Moleyns
nodes.notes: Married Robert Hungerford (1440) aged ~14; later married Sir Oliver Manyngham (1468, dau Frideswide).

nodes.name: Robert, 3rd Baron Hungerford
nodes.notes: Captured at Castillon (1453; ransomed by his mother for £9,961); Lancastrian captured at Battle of Hexham and beheaded 18 May 1464.

nodes.name: Sir Thomas Hungerford
nodes.notes: Beheaded 17 Jan 1468/69 for attempting to restore Henry VI; lands later restored to his daughter Mary under Henry VII (c. 1485).

nodes.name: Lady Mary Hungerford
nodes.notes: Married Edward, 2nd Baron Hastings (d. 1506) and later Sir Richard Sacheverell (1509).

nodes.name: Edward, 2nd Baron Hastings
nodes.notes: Husband of Hungerford heiress Lady Mary.

nodes.name: George, 1st Earl of Huntingdon
nodes.notes: Inherited Ilmer through his mother Mary Hungerford. With his son Francis, Lord Hastings, sold Ilmer manor to Sir Robert Dormer in 1538/39.

nodes.name: Francis, Lord Hastings
nodes.notes: Joined his father George in selling the manor of Ilmer to Robert Dormer in 1538/39.

nodes.name: Sir Robert Dormer
nodes.notes: Purchased the Manor of Ilmer from George & Francis Hastings in 1538/39.

nodes.name: Sir William Dormer
nodes.notes: Confirmed as titleholder c. 1553; appointed Vicars John Palmer, Swainson, and Martin Wright. Died 17 May 1575.

nodes.name: Robert, 1st Baron Dormer
nodes.notes: Knighted 1591, Baronet & Baron Dormer of Wing 1615; appointed Vicar Thomas Vaudrey in 1612.

nodes.name: Robert, 1st Earl of Carnarvon
nodes.notes: Grandson of 1st Baron Dormer; Royalist cavalry commander killed at the First Battle of Newbury on 20 Sep 1643.

nodes.name: Charles, 2nd Earl of Carnarvon
nodes.notes: Petitioned Charles II in 1660 for Ilmer & hereditary Keeper of the King’s Hawks; leased Ilmer lands to John Bowden. Died 1709 with no surviving sons.

nodes.name: Elizabeth Dormer
nodes.notes: Daughter of Charles Dormer, 2nd Earl of Carnarvon; died aged 23. Through her, the Dormer lands passed to the Stanhope Earls of Chesterfield.

nodes.name: Philip, 2nd Earl of Chesterfield
nodes.notes: Husband of Elizabeth Dormer.

nodes.name: Philip, 3rd Earl of Chesterfield
nodes.notes: Eldest grandson of Charles Dormer; inherited Ilmer in 1709.

nodes.name: Philip, 4th (d.1773) → 5th Earl (d.1815)
nodes.notes: 4th Earl (famous for Letters to his Son) adopted his cousin & godson as 5th Earl, who inherited the "Dormer Lands" including Lower, Middle & Coldharbour Farms.

members.name: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
members.notes: Author of Letters to his Son; adopted his cousin and godson as heir to the Dormer Lands.

members.name: Philip Stanhope, 5th Earl of Chesterfield
members.notes: Adopted cousin and godson of the 4th Earl; inherited the Dormer Lands including Ilmer.

nodes.name: George, 6th Earl of Chesterfield
nodes.notes: Appointed Rev. W. E. Partridge vicar of Ilmer (1833) and sold him the church patronage in 1858.

nodes.name: Rev. Richard Moreton
nodes.notes: Maternal grandfather of Moreton John Edward Frewen and grandfather of Frances Moreton-Craigie & Sister Elizabeth Moreton.

nodes.name: Dr (Rev.) Edward Frewen DD
nodes.notes: Purchased Ilmer Manor (likely at the Jul 1824 sale); succeeded by his son Moreton John Edward Frewen in Dec 1831.

nodes.name: Rev. William Moreton Moreton
nodes.notes: Uncle named in Moreton John Edward Frewen’s will; father of Frances Annabella Moreton-Craigie and Sister Elizabeth Moreton.

sources.label: Transcribed will: moreton john edward frewen

nodes.name: Moreton John Edward Frewen
nodes.notes: Married Sarah Jenkins (1812) and died childless in Jan 1871. His transcribed will left Ilmer Manor to wife Sarah for life, then to his Moreton cousins.

sources.label: Transcribed will: moreton john edward frewen

nodes.name: Frances Moreton-Craigie
nodes.notes: Eldest daughter of Rev. William Moreton Moreton; held Ilmer farms for life until her death in Feb 1892.

sources.label: Transcribed will: moreton john edward frewen

nodes.name: Sister Elizabeth Moreton
nodes.notes: Founder member of the Clewer Sisters of Mercy; funded the 1893 church restoration, 1904 farmhouses/cowsheds, 1907 Parish Room, and £100 toward the 1909 spire.

sources.label: Transcribed will: moreton john edward frewen

nodes.name: Eleanor Carter (née Frewen)
nodes.notes: Inherited Manor Farm, Lower Farm, and Coldharbour Farm on Sister Elizabeth Moreton’s death in Jan 1912 and sold the estate.
